http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/15/myste.text: At least 19 elephants have died since June in a wildlife region of southern Kenya near the Tanzanian border and Mount Kilimanjaro. The local operations head says the number has now reached 20, while authorities continue trying to establish the cause.Early tests have suggested cyanide poisoning from pesticides used on nearby farmland. But local wildlife experts say they are not convinced, as other animals feeding on the elephant carcasses have not shown signs of poisoning.According to Patrick Papatiti, head of operations for Olgulului communal lands, the elephants have reportedly suffered difficulty walking and breathing, as well as restlessness, before becoming unable to stand. "They lie down until they die. At times, you would find one struggling for a day, struggling for two or even three days until they completely die."The deaths come after Kenya experienced a severe drought in 2022, but Papatiti says current conditions do not point to a lack of food or water."Currently, we have abundant pasture around, we have water close to where these elephants go. We have protection within the ecosystem that we work."While some initial tests have suggested cyanide poisoning, Papatiti says the behaviour of scavengers around the carcasses raises questions about that explanation."We have no idea. We are still struggling with our thinking and thoughts around what is happening. We have seen hyenas eating the carcasses and they don't die. We have seen vultures feeding on the carcasses and they don't die. We have seen flies landing on the carcasses. They feast, get happy and leave. So we have no idea what this is. "The uncertainty is also raising concerns about what could happen if the cause affects other animals. "How do we know if this is going to translate into going to livestock?. Then when it gets to livestock, it is going to get to the community, local community around. So, how much are we going to lose until we fight to stop this happening?"Farmers in Kimana say they are also struggling to understand what is happening. Wildlife experts and authorities are continuing to investigate the mysterious deaths, with the cause still unresolved.

https://www.theguardian.com/business/202.text: Insulating the Bank from politics had made it better able to fulfil its role of maintaining the ‘monetary and financial conditions that make sustained prosperity possible’, Andrew Bailey said. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA View image in fullscreen Insulating the Bank from politics had made it better able to fulfil its role of maintaining the ‘monetary and financial conditions that make sustained prosperity possible’, Andrew Bailey said. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA Bank of England Populism poses serious challenge to independent central banks, Bailey says Bank of England governor says central bankers must explain decisions or risk being seen as ‘unrepresentative elite’ Heather Stewart Fri 4 Sep 2026 09.44 EDT Last modified on Fri 4 Sep 2026 10.11 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The governor of the Bank of England has said the rise of populist politicians presents a serious challenge to independent central banks. As Nigel Farage’s Reform UK gathered for its annual conference in Birmingham, Andrew Bailey said central bankers must be prepared to explain their decisions to the public or risk being attacked as an “unrepresentative elite”. Bailey was speaking at a conference at the London School of Economics . In an address peppered with historical references, from Alexander Hamilton to Thomas Hobbes, he said central banks must not take their “legitimacy for granted”. Bailey said populist parties’ pitch for power “often rests on the claim that a particular political movement alone represents the authentic will of the people. Any institution seen to get in the way becomes an unrepresentative elite standing between the people and their will, and thus an obstacle to popular sovereignty.” He added: “This is a serious challenge. We have developed systems of government (in the broadest sense of this term) in which legitimacy rests in the plurality of society, not in the preferences of any single group within it.” Populist parties, especially of the right, have been riding high on both sides of the Atlantic in recent years. Attacking traditional institutions – including central banks – often forms part of their platform. Farage has previously suggested he would like to replace Bailey if Reform comes to power. In the US, Donald Trump repeatedly launched tirades against the former Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell over the central bank’s failure to cut interest rates. View image in fullscreen Nigel Farage has previously suggested he would like to replace Andrew Bailey if Reform came to power Photograph: Thomas Krych/AP Bailey was among the international central bankers who signed a joint statement defending Powell against Trump’s criticism and stressing the importance of independence. The Bank of England was made independent by the Labour government in 1997, handing decisions on interest rates from the chancellor to a nine-member monetary policy committee (MPC) chaired by the governor. After the 2008 global financial crisis, which led to a significant proportion of the UK banking sector being nationalised at taxpayer expense, the Bank of England was given additional responsibilities for financial stability. Bailey said on Friday that insulating the Bank from politics had made it better able to fulfil its role of maintaining “the monetary and financial conditions that make sustained prosperity possible”. He said: “Institutions that exercise significant authority should expect scrutiny. Such scrutiny is a sign of democratic health. But we should also recognise what is at stake.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion The MPC is split over how to respond to rising inflation as a result of the Iran war. Bailey has stressed that in a weak jobs market, he does not yet see signs of the “second-round effects” that can embed inflation throughout the economy as workers bid up their wages to keep pace. The MPC voted to keep interest rates on hold at 3.75% at its last meeting in July. But three members voted for a rate rise, including the Bank’s hawkish chief economist, Huw Pill, who used a speech on Thursday to reiterate that in the face of rising inflation, Threadneedle Street should act “clearly, promptly and decisively”. At its next policy meeting on 17 September, the Bank is also expected to announce whether it will press ahead with its controversial policy of quantitative tightening. The Bank has been progressively selling off the bonds it acquired though the emergency policy of quantitative easing – creating money to help stave off recession. Critics, from Reform to leftwing thinktanks, have argued that these sales tend to drive up the yield, or interest rate, on government bonds, which move in the opposite direction to prices. That makes it more expensive for the government to borrow, a pressing issue at a time of febrile bond markets . Bailey will appear before MPs on the cross-party Treasury select committee next week to explain his thinking. http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/08/argen.text: The Argentine government announced on Monday that it will file a criminal complaint against several subsidiaries of the Israeli oil company Navitas for operating without authorisation in the Malvinas (Falkland Islands), which are administered by the United Kingdom but whose sovereignty is claimed by Argentina.The decision triggered an immediate reaction in Israel. The Minister for National Security, Itamar Ben Gvir, called on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to recognise Argentine sovereignty over the Malvinas and to impose sanctions on the United Kingdom "for as long as the occupation continues", accusing London of seizing Argentine territory and oil resources.According to the Argentine presidency, the complaint will target Navitas Petroleum Development & Production Ltd, Navitas Petroleum Atlantic United, Navitas Petroleum LP, JHI Associates Inc and Eco Atlantic Oil & Gas Ltd, as well as their executives and representatives.Argentina maintains that these companies "allegedly hold licences granted by the illegitimate government of the United Kingdom" to explore and exploit hydrocarbons in the North Malvinas Basin, in violation of Argentine law. The case also targets directors, managers, statutory auditors and any representatives who have taken part in the project.This is not the first time Buenos Aires has taken action over oil activity in the area. Argentina had already declared these operations illegal in 2012 and filed a similar complaint in 2015. In 2022 it sanctioned Navitas directly and, in December 2025, Javier Milei's government formally rejected investors' announcement they will pour €1.808 billion into the project to start production.Sea Lion, the oilfield at the heart of the disputeNavitas operates and controls 65% of the Sea Lion project, located around 220 kilometres north of the Falkland Islands, in waters disputed by Argentina and the United Kingdom. Its partner is the British company Rockhopper, which owns the remaining 35%. The project is in the development phase and is expected to start pumping crude oil in March 2028.The two companies had already responded to the measures announced by Argentina before the criminal complaint was submitted. Following Milei's speech last Thursday, they issued a joint statement insisting that they operate under licences "legally granted" by the islands' government and with "the full and ongoing support" of the United Kingdom.The companies stressed that they do not expect the Argentine measures to delay the Sea Lion project timeline. Rockhopper's shares fell by more than 6% on the London Stock Exchange after the announcement.Ben Gvir urges Netanyahu to recognise Argentine sovereigntyThe complaint against the subsidiaries of an Israeli oil company comes amid rising diplomatic tension between Israel and the United Kingdom. Ben Gvir called on Netanyahu to recognise Argentine sovereignty over the territory and to adopt sanctions against London "for as long as the occupation continues".The Israeli minister accused the United Kingdom of seizing territory and oil resources that, he argued, belong to the Argentine people. Hours earlier, Israel's Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, had called for the expulsion of the British ambassador to Israel.The remarks come amid widening rifts between London and Tel Aviv over British policy towards Palestine. For the moment, Ben Gvir's words do not amount to a change in Israel's official position on the islands' sovereignty.Milei steps up his offensivePresident Javier Milei announced on Thursday that he intends to toughen sanctions on oil companies operating in the Falkland Islands under licences issued by the British territory. He also said he would send a bill to Congress that would extend sanctions to the suppliers of these companies and bar offenders from contracting with the Argentine state.That same day he confirmed that he will revive plans to build a naval base in Ushuaia, around 700 kilometres from the islands. On Monday, Milei instructed Economy Minister Luis Caputo to give the project priority in the 2027 budget, which the government will send to Congress this month."These measures are part of a comprehensive policy aimed at strengthening the Argentine state's ability to defend its territory, protect its natural resources and safeguard its strategic interests," the government said in a statement.

Photo: Camilla Stephan / Louisiana Museum of Modern Art. HUMLEBÆK .- The Spanish-Mexican painter Remedios Varo (1908-1963) is the subject of a major retrospective opening at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in Denmark on 18 September, marking the first presentation of her work on this scale in Europe. In recent years, Varo has attracted renewed attention as one of Surrealism’s most original figures and a pioneering feminist artist. The exhibition features the artist’s most significant works on loan from museums in Mexico and the US alongside key works from private collections that are rarely exhibited publicly. With her singular blend of precision and poetry, Remedios Varo conjures a Surrealist world of mysterious musicians, eccentric scientists, strange contraptions and enigmatic travellers inhabiting imaginary landscapes and uncanny interiors. Visitors can explore her captivating images in the Louisiana’s upcoming exhibition, a timely introduction to an artist who remains largely unknown in Northern Europe. “The dream world and the real world are the same,” declared Remedios Varo, who is known for alchemically combining traditional techniques and Surrealist methods with mystical philosophical inquiry into visionary narratives. Her style – exact, meticulous and classical – reaches back to late medieval and early Renaissance painting. Varo was a curious and exploratory artist who drew inspiration from a wide range of fields of knowledge, including alchemy, astronomy, quantum physics, psychology, technological innovation, esoteric traditions and spiritual practices. With meticulous technical precision, she created a universe in which the cosmic and the everyday converge with dreamlike openness and disarming humour. Her works challenge our perception of reality, making it difficult to tell whether we are looking into a distant past or a world yet to come. Varo was also unequivocally a feminist, articulating a unique Surrealist vocabulary rooted in female experience and ideas of feminine creativity and self-determination. Challenging traditional notions of women’s place in society, she envisioned forms of female spirituality and intellectual autonomy. The exhibition will present 70 works, complemented by photographs, notebooks and personal artefacts, spanning from Varo’s early years in Barcelona and Paris to her to her peak productive period in Mexico in the 1950s and 1960s. While broadly chronological in structure, the exhibition also highlights key themes and lines of development of Varo’s artistic practice. In 2020, five works by Varo were showcased in the Louisiana’s Fantastic Women exhibition, a presentation of women Surrealists. María de los Remedios Alicia Rodriga Varo y Uranga was born in northern Spain in 1908 and grew up in a home with a devout Catholic mother and a father who was a hydraulic engineer and a freethinker. He taught her how to draw and supported her desire to become an artist. At 15, she became one of the first women admitted to the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Madrid. In the 1920s, she rubbed elbows with local avant-garde artists, including the poet and playwright Federico García Lorca, the film director Luis Buñuel and the artist Salvador Dalí. Because of the growing political unrest in Spain in the 1930s, she moved to Paris, where she joined the Surrealist circle. After the Nazi invasion of Paris, she fled to Marseille and was among the artists rescued from France in 1941. Varo settled in Mexico City with her partner, the Surrealist poet Benjamin Péret, becoming part of a vibrant community of Mexican and European artists inspired by Mexico’s culture and landscape. Alongside her painting, she initially made a living by producing commercial illustrations, restoring pre-Columbian art and decorating furniture. In the early 1950s, she began a relationship with the Austrian émigré Walter Gruen, which gave her the freedom to dedicate herself to her painting without financial concern. Her closest friends – and collaborators – were the British artist Leonora Carrington and the Hungarian photojournalist Kati Horna. Her first solo exhibition in 1956 proved a decisive artistic breakthrough. The exhibition was met with critical acclaim, every work sold within days, and demand for her paintings was such that collectors joined waiting lists. Just a few years later, in 1963, Varo died suddenly at the age of 54, at the peak of her career. André Breton described her as “a sorceress who left us too soon”. https://bnn-news.com/politics/after-stab.text: Aleksejs Rosļikovs · Photo: Lita Millere/LETA Advertisements Following the election result in which Stability! received 1.997% of the vote, failing to enter the Saeima and losing state funding, party leader Aleksejs Rosļikovs currently has no plans to return to Latvia from Belarus, party board chair Svetlana Čulkova told LETA. At the same time, Čulkova said Rosļikovs does not intend to end his political activities. “He will continue to be actively involved in politics, express his views and defend the people and issues to which he has devoted his work so far,” the politician said. Čulkova thanked those who supported Stability! in the Saeima election. Advertisements “Despite everything that has happened recently, despite the pressure directed against our party, against me and against Aleksejs Rosļikovs, you still came out and cast your vote for us,” the Saeima member said, noting that it had not been an easy period. Čulkova noted that before the election Rosļikovs had clearly stated that if people in Latvia supported him and were prepared to stand up for him, he would be ready to return to Latvia. “The election results currently show that society has a different view of Latvia’s future direction. Voters did not choose the political course we proposed – more active defence of residents’ interests, improving prosperity, lower prices, greater social security and protecting the interests of Latvia’s residents,” Čulkova said. According to the party, the result also shows that a large part of society is currently not prepared to stand up more actively for its interests and demand changes that would improve people’s everyday lives and well-being. Advertisements “That is society’s decision, and in a democracy it must be respected,” Čulkova said. Stability! accepts the election result as it stands. At the same time, the party says its convictions remain unchanged. Latvia’s residents deserve a better standard of living, more affordable prices, social security and policies that put people and their well-being first, Čulkova said. She added that the party would continue its work. As reported, the Central Election Commission (CVK) has compiled the preliminary results of the 15th Saeima election held on 3 October. According to the preliminary data, 806,641 voters, or 51.79% of eligible voters, participated in the election. The United List received the largest share of the vote, with 35.288%. It was followed by Latvia First with 13.076% and Sovereign Power/Young Latvians with 11.710%. Advertisements The National Alliance also crossed the 5% threshold with 8.897%, followed by the Progressives with 7.878% and New Unity with 6.362%. The Union of Greens and Farmers failed to cross the 5% threshold, receiving 4.401% of the vote. We Are Changing the Rules received 3.428%, Latvia’s Development 2.179%, while Stability! received 1.997%. Rising Sun for Latvia received 1.330%, Gobzems’ List 0.982%, the Harmony Centre political alliance 0.820%, and the New Conservative Party (JKP) 0.327%. The CVK stresses that the published results are preliminary and that the final election results will be approved at a CVK meeting. As previously reported, vote counting has now been completed at all polling stations in Latvia and by all postal voting commissions. Zelensky also said Kyiv is sourcing F-16 ammunition around the world, with new packages already on the way. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 6, 2026, 2:30 am Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied In this handout photograph taken and released by the Ukrainian Presidential Press Service on September 30, 2026, President Volodymyr Zelensky attends a meeting with Ukrainian servicemen at an undisclosed frontline location near Lyman, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN PRESIDENTIAL PRESS SERVICE / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Ukraine is moving to strengthen its air defenses as Kyiv races to shield critical infrastructure against intensifying Russian strikes, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday. “We are preparing new contracts for air defense systems and missiles,” Zelensky said during his evening address , adding that details remain under wraps but “there may be some positive steps.” JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . According to the Ukrainian leader, Kyiv is strengthening its defenses daily with additional gun turrets, specialized Shahed-hunting teams and increased production of interceptor systems. “We expect manufacturers to move quickly on interceptors. The tasks have been defined, and the funding is available,” Zelensky said. The Ukrainian president also appealed to Kyiv’s international partners for additional anti-ballistic capabilities, describing the protection of critical infrastructure as the country’s most pressing air-defense challenge. Advertisement “We need more anti-ballistic capabilities to protect infrastructure specifically. This is the main challenge right now,” he said. The push comes after Ukraine and Germany signed 15 defense agreements worth more than €8.5 billion ($9.6 billion) on Sunday, covering air defense missiles, drones, radar systems, Patriot ammunition and protection of Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. Kyiv has also previously signed contracts for approximately 1,000 Patriot missiles, while Germany pledged additional interceptors from its own military stocks. The effort is aimed at strengthening Ukraine’s missile reserves as Russia continues targeting the country’s energy and civilian infrastructure. Global search for F-16 ammunition Alongside ground-based air defenses, Ukraine is searching worldwide for ammunition for its F-16 fighter jets. Zelensky described the US-made aircraft as one of Ukraine’s most effective tools for intercepting Russia’s jet-powered Shahed drones. “We are now sourcing munitions for F-16s virtually all over the world,” Zelensky said. “Packages are already on the way, and there will be more, so that our aircraft have what they need to protect our cities.” Advertisement To suggest a correction or clarification, write to us here You can also highlight the text and press Ctrl + Enter Contact Us Please leave your suggestions or corrections here Cancel Send Kyiv Post Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995.
